public_rationale: The evidence shows both substantial difficulty and meaningful late-2025 progress. VideoGameBench tests different objectives and earlier models. SIMA 2 and NitroGen show broader capability, but neither establishes the full rapid-learning claim. These records do not justify turning selected failures into proof of non-arrival, or selected successes into proof of near-universal competence.
limitations: The source does not define almost any, basic mastery, or the exact learning-time limit.
The strongest late-year evidence is developer research rather than a matched independent comparison.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Marcus seriously doubts that AI will be able, by the end of 2025, to learn and master the basics of almost any new video game within a few minutes or hours and solve original puzzles in that game's world.
conditions: within a few minutes or hours

statement.excerpt: Learn and master the basics of almost any new video game within a few minutes or hours, and solve original puzzles in the alternate world of that video game.

from_speaker: within a few minutes or hours
our_interpretation: Read this as a directional forecast against broad, rapid competence in unfamiliar games, including solving their original puzzles.
New means unfamiliar to the tested agent; it need not mean commercially released after the post.
Mastering basics does not require completing an entire game.
Almost any requires broad coverage across game types, but the source supplies no percentage.
The task descriptions are success criteria, not external antecedents.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of systems available through the deadline show persistent failures to learn ordinary game basics and solve original puzzles within minutes or a few hours across a broad range of unfamiliar games.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system available by the deadline demonstrates those abilities across a broad, representative set of unfamiliar games under the stated learning-time allowance.

evidence.publisher: Zhang, Griffiths, Narasimhan and Press, via arXiv
evidence.explanation: VideoGameBench documents substantial difficulties in ten games. Its May models and whole-game objectives do not establish the status of rapid basic learning at the December deadline.

SIMA 2 demonstrates meaningful transfer to unfamiliar games, including ASKA and MineDojo. The study does not establish mastery and original-puzzle solving across almost any new game within the claimed learning window.

NitroGen broadens game-playing capability, but the report identifies limitations in planning and following language instructions. It does not supply the required timed, broad unfamiliar-game learning evaluation.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reproducible evaluation of systems available by December 31, 2025 on representative unfamiliar games, documenting learning time, basic mastery, and original-puzzle performance against ordinary human learners.
